minutes.headline: Select Board voted to write off the ambulance receivables and delayed the revenue turnover policy vote one week.
minutes.summary: The board heard the water district on PFAS, ratified a police officer and other appointments, and heard the DPW director on Chapter 90 funds and drainage plans. It voted to write off old ambulance receivables after questions about liens and Medicare adjustments. It also got a quarterly financial report, reviewed the town meeting consent calendar, and discussed the Agricultural Commission not meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to write off old ambulance receivables as presented, after questions about liens and Medicare adjustments.
The board delayed the revenue turnover policy one week and asked that it be distributed to other boards in the meantime.
The DPW director described Chapter 90 road funds, a large unspent balance, and a request for milling and paving on several roads.
The board accepted the town meeting consent calendar as drafted, with no articles pulled.
The board ratified a full-time police officer appointment, plus a facilities custodian, a beach director and two seasonal lifeguards.

why_it_matters: Writing off ambulance receivables removes old billed amounts the town was carrying as owed, so it bears on how much ambulance revenue the town can count on collecting.
The consent calendar covers stabilization transfers, OPEB, enterprise budgets and prior-year bills, which residents will be asked to vote on together at town meeting unless an article is pulled.
The revenue turnover policy, which sets how revenue is handled, is still undecided, and other boards will see it before the Select Board votes.
watch_next: The revenue turnover policy returns at the Select Board's next meeting, one week out.
The town meeting consent calendar, as drafted, goes to the floor with no articles pulled.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all four votes and most decisions. Remaining differences are mostly caption errors in figures and names, plus details only one side recorded. The one thing to check is the Chapter 90 "balance" ($890,000 in ours vs. $890,954 spent and $2,002,925 remaining in the official minutes), along with the speaker role label for "Mr. Jeff".
